title: Department Hearing Office Room Block Schedule — Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
Three appellant exhibits and sixty minutes of docket hearing time are the two thresholds of the room block gap for in-person sessions of Unemployment Insurance Appeals at the Department hearing office. An in-person session is placed a number of calendar days after the hearing date set on the appeal; that number is the *room block gap*. It turns on how many exhibits the appellant has submitted on the appeal and on the hearing length of the appeal's docket.

**Schedule.** The room block gap is the long room block days when at least the exhibit threshold of exhibits submitted by the appellant stand received on the appeal and the docket's hearing length is at least the long session minutes, the short room block days when at least the exhibit threshold of such exhibits stand received and the docket's hearing length is shorter than the long session minutes, and the standard room block days when fewer than the exhibit threshold of exhibits submitted by the appellant stand received.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Exhibit threshold | 3 exhibits submitted by the appellant |
| Long session threshold | 60 minutes |
| Long room block | 12 calendar days |
| Short room block | 6 calendar days |
| Standard room block | 4 calendar days |

## The gap as a matrix

| Appellant's exhibits received on the appeal | Docket hearing length 60 minutes or more | Docket hearing length under 60 minutes |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | 12 days | 6 days |
| 2 or fewer | 4 days | 4 days |

## By docket

The docket hearing lengths are: Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue 60 minutes; Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue 45; Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination 45; Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud 60; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge 60; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate 90; Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review 0 (no hearing). With 3 or more appellant exhibits, the gap is therefore 12 days on the Separation Issue, Overpayment and Fraud, Employer Benefit Charge and Employer Contribution Rate dockets and 6 days on the Able and Available Issue and Monetary Determination dockets.

## Points of judgement

- Only exhibits the **appellant** submitted count — every one recorded as received from the appellant, whether it met the exhibit deadline or was recorded as late. The other party's exhibits do not count.
- *Boundaries:* exactly 3 appellant exhibits reach the threshold, 2 do not; a hearing length of exactly 60 minutes is at least the long session minutes.

*Hypothetical cases:* an employer appellant on the Employer Contribution Rate docket with 4 exhibits — 12 days; a claimant appellant on the Monetary Determination docket with 3 exhibits — 6 days; a claimant appellant with 2 exhibits while the employer filed 5 — 4 days.
